senses.sense_definition: Relating to the Afroasiatic subfamily of languages including Arabic, Hebrew, Amharic, and Aramaic.

examples.text: Arabic and Hebrew both belong to the <w>Semitic</w> language family.
The professor specialized in ancient <w>Semitic</w> scripts and grammar.

senses.sense_definition: Relating to Semites, historically comprising various peoples of southwestern Asia.

examples.text: Ancient history books describe early migrations of various <w>Semitic</w> tribes across the region.
Archaeologists uncovered artifacts belonging to early <w>Semitic</w> settlements in the desert.

senses.sense_definition: Relating to religions that originated among Semitic peoples, particularly the Abrahamic faiths.

examples.text: The theology course compared traditions found among the major <w>Semitic</w> religions.
Monotheism is a central feature common to these historic <w>Semitic</w> faiths.

senses.sense_definition: Relating to the descendants of Shem according to biblical tradition.

examples.text: Medieval scholars often grouped ancient nations according to their supposed <w>Semitic</w> descent.
In the biblical table of nations, several kingdoms are described as having <w>Semitic</w> origins.

senses.sense_definition: Relating to Jewish, Hebrew, or Israeli people.

examples.text: The author reflected on her <w>Semitic</w> heritage and cultural traditions.
Certain cultural institutions were established to preserve classical <w>Semitic</w> literature.

traits.comment: Now largely replaced by specific terms like Jewish or Hebrew

senses.sense_definition: The branch of the Afroasiatic language family that includes Arabic, Hebrew, and related tongues.

examples.text: The linguistics department offers advanced courses in Comparative <w>Semitic</w>.
Scholars believe that Proto <w>Semitic</w> originated somewhere in the Middle East.
